objective: TIME-POLISH PPO on Jungle8: start from the bc49 panorama BC student that won 7 of its 8 held-out panorama seeds (hold 8, seeds 1495002000..1495002007; lineage.bc_champion_panorama_eval8 - the eighth episode was a time-limit TRUNCATION at 30000 ticks, not a terminated loss: the policy survived the full horizon without clearing) and optimize EXPECTED COMPLETION TIME, replicating the recipe that just WORKED on Jungle1 (lineage.recipe_validation: tier_1, student median 3058 beat teacher 3134 at 16/16, concluded by the preregistered stagnation clause). HONEST EVIDENCE DELTA versus the Jungle1 premise: the Jungle1 init carried a 10,000-seed tail receipt (98.56% win rate); this init carries an 8-seed receipt (7/8, point estimate 87.5%). Seven wins bound the true win rate only loosely, so the clause (a) win-rate floor is doing correspondingly more of the safety work here than it did on Jungle1 - if the floor fires, the honest reading is that the init's win rate was never high enough for time-polish, which is itself a reportable lateral-expansion finding. All seven panorama wins finished under this run's 12000-tick training horizon (fastest 3179, median 8036), so the win evidence survives the max_ticks 30000 -> 12000 protocol change intact; only the truncated episode would have truncated sooner. The premise stands on the validated Jungle1 mechanism: when the +10 win bonus appears in most episodes, the return's residual variance is dominated by the 5x time term (-0.0005/native tick) and PPO polishes speed instead of searching for wins. Success is measured in median winning ticks at a win-rate floor; SCORE IS NOT A SUCCESS METRIC.

reward_resolution.ordering_guarantees: the composed training wrapper is DenseShapingObservableHumanSpeedrunWrapper; its _validate_reward_ordering enforces minimum win return > maximum terminated-failure return: (10 + (-0.0005 x 12000)) = +4.0 > (-10 + 1.0) = -9.0, satisfied with margin 13.0 at Jungle8's max_ticks 12000 (identical arithmetic to the pattern: jungle levels are not in the long-horizon prefix list). The base-wrapper one-second dominance rule is deliberately dropped by the v2 dense-shaping mixin, exactly as documented in the pattern.
reward_resolution.magnitude_rationale: 5x clock signal, unchanged from the validated recipe. At the panorama win median (~8036 ticks, hold 8, max_ticks 30000) the time term would cost ~-4.0 against +10; at the training horizon the worst POSSIBLE win costs -6.0, still netting +4.0, so winning strictly dominates everything and the residual gradient on winning episodes is the clock. A 500-tick speedup is worth +0.25 per episode, the same well-posed polish signal that took Jungle1 from median 3833 to 3058. The stall mode observed on panorama seed 1495002001 is exactly what the clock term punishes: a truncated stall returns about -6.0 + at most +1.0 shaping, strictly below every win.

clause_a_win_rate_floor.clause: if the 16-seed eval win rate is below 0.90 (i.e. 14/16 or fewer wins) at TWO CONSECUTIVE checkpoints, STOP the run and keep the best earlier checkpoint
clause_a_win_rate_floor.best_checkpoint_rule: best = highest 16-seed win rate; ties broken by lower median winning ticks; the BC init itself is the fallback if no checkpoint qualifies (HONEST NOTE: the init has no receipt on this 16-seed panel - its 7/8 evidence is on the panorama block 1495002000..1495002007 - so the fallback is 'the only receipted winner on this level', not 'a panel-benchmarked baseline'; the first checkpoint eval doubles as the panel baseline)
clause_a_win_rate_floor.rationale: with a 7/8 init (point estimate 87.5%, already below the 0.90 floor on its own tiny sample), the floor is doing MORE work here than on Jungle1 and may legitimately fire early if the init's true win rate is materially below ~0.9; that outcome is reported as 'init not polish-ready', a real lateral-expansion finding, not massaged away. Two consecutive sub-0.90 panels is the same preregistered trigger that protected the Jungle1 run

clause_b_stagnation_success.clause: if the median winning ticks of the 16-seed eval fails to improve on the best median observed so far at THREE CONSECUTIVE checkpoint evals, CONCLUDE THE RUN SUCCESSFULLY with the best checkpoint
clause_b_stagnation_success.best_checkpoint_rule: best = lowest median winning ticks among checkpoints whose 16-seed win rate is >= 0.90
clause_b_stagnation_success.rationale: time-polish saturates; three flat checkpoints (~786k steps) is the preregistered definition of converged. This clause is no longer a hypothesis: it fired on Jungle1 exactly as designed (checkpoints 1834k/2096k/2359k flat against 1572k's 3058) and banked the champion

trainer_v2.reward_alignment: cap 1.0 and the 5x time term carried unchanged from the validated recipe. Arithmetic at Jungle8's max_ticks 12000: worst win = 10 - 6.0 = +4.0; best truncation (truncation-neutral) = about -6.0 + 1.0 = -5.0; best terminated failure = -10 + 1.0 - time < -9.0. Ordering: every win > every truncation > every terminated failure; on winning episodes the clock is the dominant residual signal, which is the entire point of this run.
trainer_v2.discounting_note: gamma applies PER MACRO STEP; the macro reward is the undiscounted per-tick sum over the ticks the macro consumed, so 0.999 per macro is roughly 0.999^(1/40) per native tick; truncation is reward-neutral (v2 wrapper), so a timed-out episode bootstraps instead of paying -10
